units.title: Behavioral specifications, policy boundaries and threat models
outcomes: Separate intended behavior, observed compliance and unresolved policy choices.
Map an LLM application's assets, actors, access, trust boundaries and residual consequences to testable claims.
Specify expected behavior for benign, ambiguous and disallowed requests before labeling outputs.
units.why: The Systems unit on security goals, trust boundaries and threat models taught system threat modeling. Here the new job is to connect a model behavior to a plausible harm and a measurable policy boundary, not just draw the system.

next.note: Measure both sides of the policy boundary.

study.title: OpenAI Model Spec, 2026-08-18: one worked behavior contract
study.locator: Instructions and levels of authority; The chain of command, especially Follow all applicable instructions and Ignore untrusted data by default; Protect people's privacy
study.depth: Read these sections and their examples only. Treat the vendor's choices as an example, not a universal policy or evidence of compliance.

study.title: ARENA 3.1: Threat-Modeling & Specification Design
study.locator: What are evals trying to achieve?; Threat-Modeling; Specification; Question Design
study.depth: Work by hand. Skip hosted API calls and the alignment-faking replication.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: policy and threat-model ownership
study.locator: Section 3, GOVERN 3.2: GV-3.2-003 (acceptable use and refusal criteria) and GV-3.2-005 (threat modeling)

focus: Write the deployment scope first: a local assistant with offline documents and no real credentials or external actions. Name who can edit user messages, retrieved text and tool results.
Give every test a policy clause, expected behavior, severity and rationale. Clarification and safe assistance are distinct from refusal.
Connect each threat to an asset, attacker capability, entry point, mitigation, detection signal and residual consequence. Record assumptions the experiment cannot test.
Freeze the specification before labels. Keep disputed normative cases visible rather than relabeling them to match a benchmark.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, trace a fake instruction in a retrieved document through an offline assistant to an unauthorized disclosure of a synthetic secret. Mark the authority boundary, then write one benign request, one ambiguous request and one disallowed request with expected behavior and the policy clause that decides each.
traps: Calling a specification an empirical safety result. It states what should happen; the campaign measures what actually happens.
Treating a model's stated intentions or multiple-choice answer as proof of its motives. Measure behavior under a stated protocol instead.
Letting the benchmark silently define policy. Its labels may disagree with your intended application.

selfTest.q: A retrieved page says it is a system message. Does that grant it authority?
selfTest.a: No. Its provenance remains untrusted retrieved data. A textual claim of authority does not change the message's trust boundary.

selfTest.q: Why keep ambiguous requests in the specification?
selfTest.a: They test clarification and context-sensitive assistance. A binary refuse-or-comply policy can hide both unsafe completions and unnecessary refusals.

selfTest.q: A test passes, but its assumed tool permission is absent in the application. What follows?
selfTest.a: The result describes that test configuration, not the proposed harm pathway. Reconcile the access assumption before using it in the safety argument.

practice.name: ARENA 3.1: Build threat models; Design a specification
practice.locator: Exercises Build threat models and Design a specification
practice.note: Adapt one property to your offline assistant. Write the causal scenario and operational definitions by hand; no paid API is needed. Keep the assumptions and unresolved choices for the campaign.

units.stopWhen: Your written scope and policy decide the three boundary cases, and every modeled threat ends in a testable claim or an owned evidence gap.

fit.note: The dated Model Spec, ARENA design exercises and NIST actions cover the policy, threat and ownership job without a new resource.

units.title: Harmful capability versus harmful compliance, refusal and overrefusal
outcomes: Measure harmful compliance, refusal and benign overrefusal as separate outcomes.
Distinguish failed elicitation from evidence that a model lacks a capability.
Diagnose a safety-score gain caused by indiscriminate refusal or degraded answer quality.
units.why: A model can stop saying refusal phrases without producing useful harmful content. It can also improve a safety score by refusing everything. This unit establishes the two-sided baseline for the campaign.

next.note: Check whether the instrument can distinguish these outcomes.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 5 supplement, Version 26.0.0
study.locator: Sections 3.4 and 5.4: SimpleSafetyTests before and after SFT, problems `sst_baseline` and `sst_sft`
study.depth: Keep the before/after protocol, not the large models or hosted setup. Use the small-model substitute in Practice and hand labels instead of the 70B grader.

study.title: XSTest: safe and unsafe contrast prompts
study.locator: README, Using XSTest; `xstest_prompts.csv`, columns `id`, `type` and `label`; `evaluation/classify_completions_strmatch.py`

study.title: StrongREJECT, arXiv:2402.10260v1
study.locator: Section 2.2, Response evaluation; Section 3.4, Our StrongREJECT autograder; Sections 6.2 and 6.3 on capability degradation
study.depth: Study the rubric and controls. Do not run its paid or gated graders.

focus: The pinned XSTest table has 250 safe prompts and 200 unsafe contrast prompts. Preserve row IDs and report denominators separately; a small subset is not the full benchmark.
Label refusal, policy violation and useful assistance separately. A disclaimer followed by a disallowed answer remains a violation; a harmless off-topic answer is not useful compliance.
Use the written policy to adjudicate borderline cases. Review offensive or distressing examples privately and stop review when needed; do not publish raw harmful generations.
Freeze checkpoint, template, decoding, token budget and item IDs across comparisons. Failed generations remain in the ledger with explicit status.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, construct a score table for an always-refuse assistant and an always-answer assistant on your policy-labeled safe and unsafe slices. The first has complete overrefusal on safe requests and no harmful compliance if its refusals contain no disallowed content. The second's harmful-compliance rate still depends on what its answers actually contain, not just the absence of refusal words.
traps: Calling non-refusal an attack success. StrongREJECT checks whether the answer actually addresses the harmful goal.
Calling failure on one prompt proof of absent capability. Prompting, output budget and model comprehension can all limit elicitation.
Using XSTest's string labels as policy truth. Its prefix matcher has no partial-compliance category and can mistake an apology for a full refusal.

selfTest.q: Can refusal rate rise while useful safety gets worse?
selfTest.a: Yes. Benign requests may be refused more often while harmful completions persist. Inspect both slices and the content of each answer.

selfTest.q: An encoded attack produces nonsense rather than a refusal. Is it successful?
selfTest.a: Not on that evidence. Non-refusal alone does not establish useful harmful assistance; the encoding may have destroyed comprehension.

selfTest.q: Why not pool the safe and unsafe denominators?
selfTest.a: Their desired behaviors differ. A pooled score changes with the slice mixture and can hide benign utility loss.

practice.name: CS336 supplement: `sst_baseline` and `sst_sft`, reduced-scale adaptation
practice.locator: Sections 3.4 and 5.4; retain prompts, raw generations and item-level scores
practice.note: Use your existing small SFT checkpoint and its parent. Otherwise use HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct at revision 12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac as a single baseline, with transformers 5.19 and PyTorch 2.14.1. Generate a preselected small harm-area-balanced SimpleSafetyTests subset and a type-balanced XSTest subset on your GPU or CPU, one request at a time. Record the chat template and a fixed short output budget. Hand-score both; there are no public safety-label tests. Do not claim an SFT effect without two related checkpoints. The handouts and tests are public study material; never publish course solutions.

units.stopWhen: Your baseline report separates harmful compliance, safe-prompt overrefusal and useful benign answers, with item IDs, raw outputs, failure counts and a stated elicitation limit.

fit.note: The CS336 experiment, pinned XSTest and StrongREJECT rubric jointly cover compliance, overrefusal and capability confounds at small scale.

units.title: Jailbreak, prompt-injection and multi-turn attacks, and adaptive red teaming
outcomes: Implement a bounded adaptive attack loop with complete query and feedback provenance.
Distinguish direct jailbreaks, indirect injection and target-side multi-turn attacks.
Measure mitigation generalization on attack families excluded from development.
units.why: The Systems unit on tenant isolation, input validation and injection covered classic injection. LLM attacks add natural-language instruction conflicts and adaptive feedback, so a fixed prompt list cannot establish resistance to a changing attacker.

next.note: Retest defenses against an attacker allowed to adapt.

study.title: Indirect prompt injection, arXiv:2302.12173v1
study.locator: Figures 1 and 2; Section 3, Attack Surface of Application-Integrated Large Language Models; Section 4, Discussion on the Validity of Attacks
study.depth: Read the trust boundaries and synthetic application, not the product demonstrations as current vulnerabilities. Never target a live third-party system.

study.title: PAIR, arXiv:2310.08419v1
study.locator: Section 3, especially Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4
study.depth: Reconstruct one serial stream. Skip published multi-model sweeps and hosted attackers or judges.

study.title: CS336 supplement: red-team after instruction tuning
study.locator: Section 5.5, problem `red_teaming`

focus: A direct jailbreak tries to override policy through the user's request. Indirect injection arrives through lower-trust retrieved content. Multi-turn attacks preserve target conversation state; record it explicitly.
PAIR retains attacker history but normally gives the target a fresh candidate prompt. Do not describe that alone as target-side multi-turn evaluation.
Retain parent attack ID, source, family, edits, feedback, target checkpoint, full transcript, query count and token budget. Count unsuccessful and malformed attempts too.
Split by attack family and source before tuning. Freeze the defense, then allow a fresh, budget-matched adaptation on held-out families without changing the defense again.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, draw one PAIR stream from candidate to target response to judged feedback to revised candidate. Then contrast it with a target conversation that retains earlier turns. Give each an explicit stopping budget and show which transcript must be restored to replay an unsuccessful attempt.
traps: Reporting only the winning prompt. Selection consumed failed queries and can overstate a method's efficiency.
Counting paraphrases of a training attack as held-out families. Shared templates and sources can leak across the split.
Using a fake secret copied into the attack itself as extraction evidence. Success must require crossing the boundary, not echoing attacker-supplied text.

selfTest.q: Two attacks each succeed once, but one uses more retries. Are their success rates comparable?
selfTest.a: Not without a common budget and success unit. Report success per behavior under the same query and token limits, plus the cost of all attempts.

selfTest.q: Does an attacker editing a retrieved document need control of the user's prompt?
selfTest.a: No. Retrieval can carry attacker text into the assistant even when the user makes an ordinary request.

selfTest.q: Why rerun an adaptive attacker after installing a defense?
selfTest.a: A defense may only block known strings. Fresh feedback tests whether the attacker can route around it within the declared budget.

practice.name: CS336 supplement: `red_teaming`, local adaptive extension
practice.note: Use the frozen small checkpoint and software from the earlier unit on harmful compliance and overrefusal. Bound one stream to five target queries per behavior; act as the attacker by hand and hand-check feedback. Include direct, offline retrieved-text and target-history cases using invented policy violations only. Disable network tools and real credentials. This is a reduced manual adaptation, not a PAIR replication. Keep regression fixtures for the query cap and transcript replay; the course has no public attack-success tests. Never publish course solutions.

units.stopWhen: You can replay every attempt, enforce the declared budget, and report static versus adaptive outcomes on a family-held-out slice with all failures retained.

fit.note: The injection paper supplies trust boundaries, PAIR supplies the feedback loop, and the named CS336 exercise anchors bounded local practice.

units.title: Memorization, training-data extraction and sensitive-information leakage
outcomes: Measure extraction of planted synthetic canaries under a declared access and query budget.
Separate training-data memorization, prefix-assisted discovery and leakage from the current context.
Explain why a failed extraction attempt and low perplexity alone cannot establish a privacy guarantee.
units.why: The Systems unit on membership inference, extraction, inversion and poisoning and the LLM Foundations unit on contamination and memorization introduced the attacks. The new evidence is controlled exposure in your own training pipeline, not searching a pretrained model for real people's records.

next.note: Carry exposure limits and untested privacy risks into the release decision.

study.title: Carlini et al., USENIX Security 2021 proceedings
study.locator: Section 3, Threat Model & Ethics, especially Definitions 1 and 2, Section 3.2 threat model and Section 3.4 ethics; Section 5.2, Improved Membership Inference
study.depth: Study the generation-and-ranking method, but replace all real-data discovery and validation with your own invented canaries. Do not reproduce Internet searches for personal records.

study.title: Nasr et al., arXiv:2311.17035v1
study.locator: Section 1, Ethics & Responsible Disclosure; Section 3.1, Prior Approaches and Definitions; Section 3.5, Discoverable Mem. vs. Extractable Mem.
study.depth: Stop at the definitions and limits. Production-endpoint attacks and large-corpus searches are not practice.

focus: Plant invented random strings in a known number of training documents. Track document multiplicity separately from repeated occurrences and actual token exposure.
Use an untouched checkpoint and untrained canaries as controls. Keep all secret suffixes out of prompts, retrieval, judge instructions and logs exposed to the target.
Predeclare byte-exact suffix matching, prefix lengths, decoding and total attempts. Report prefix-assisted and unprompted results separately, including negative results.
Perplexity or a reference-model ratio ranks candidates; it does not prove membership. Matching a known planted suffix supplies ground truth for this experiment only.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, design a canary experiment with a training-exposed string, an untrained control string and an unchanged checkpoint. Specify which prefix the attacker knows and which suffix must be generated. Draw a separate path for a synthetic secret present only in retrieved context, and explain why that path tests context leakage rather than training memorization.
traps: Scoring tokens supplied in the prefix as extracted content. Score only the withheld suffix and record how much context the attack received.
Interpreting non-extraction as non-memorization. A finite attack can miss stored information or lack a suitable prompt.
Assuming public information has no privacy risk. Reproduction in a new context can violate contextual integrity.

selfTest.q: A canary occurs ten times in one training document. Is its document multiplicity ten?
selfTest.a: No. It is one document under the paper's definition. Repeated occurrences and token exposure are separate experimental quantities.

selfTest.q: A low-perplexity completion looks like an address. Does it prove extraction?
selfTest.a: No. It may be common, fabricated or inferable. This exercise verifies only exact matches to known synthetic training records.

selfTest.q: Why compare with an unchanged checkpoint?
selfTest.a: It helps distinguish an effect of your planted-data training from pre-existing completion behavior. It does not by itself prove that every observed difference is memorization.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a bounded synthetic-canary exposure study on your existing tiny decoder, with an unchanged checkpoint, untrained canaries, withheld suffixes, complete query records and a separate synthetic context-leakage test. Reuse the recorded training stack; CPU with a smaller decoder is sufficient. No real personal data or production endpoint is involved.
units.stopWhen: Your privacy evidence distinguishes exposure from discovery, includes controls and failed queries, and states exactly which matching rule and attack budget the result supports.

fit.note: Carlini supplies the threat and ranking method; Nasr supplies the discoverability distinction. The campaign supplies controlled synthetic-only practice.

units.title: Bias, representation and disparate errors across affected-group slices
outcomes: Measure ambiguous and disambiguated BBQ outcomes separately, with affected-group support counts.
Distinguish representational harm from disparate task errors and option-order artifacts.
State what one US-English benchmark category cannot establish about fairness.
units.why: The Classical ML unit on learning curves, error taxonomies and slices taught slice reporting. Here the new job is to test whether stereotypes replace missing evidence or override supplied evidence, not merely to find a low-scoring subgroup.

next.note: Keep group-specific regressions visible when comparing mitigations.

study.title: BBQ, Findings of ACL 2022 proceedings
study.locator: Sections 3 to 5: coverage, template construction, validation, accuracy and bias scores; Figure 1's ambiguous/disambiguated contrast

study.title: BBQ data and metadata contract
study.locator: README, File structure and Models; `data`, `templates` and `supplemental/additional_metadata.csv`
study.depth: Choose one category and a small template-balanced subset. Preserve both context conditions and question polarities; do not reproduce the full model sweep.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: bias beyond one benchmark
study.locator: Section 2.6, Harmful Bias and Homogenization

focus: An ambiguous context supports the unknown answer. A disambiguated context supplies evidence for a person. Always choosing unknown trades stereotype avoidance for task failure.

Join metadata by category and example ID, not example ID alone. Use the bias target and question polarity to identify stereotype-aligned outputs; an incorrect answer is not automatically stereotype-aligned.
Report accuracy, unknown-answer rate, invalid outputs, support and bias score separately by context. Undefined conditional scores stay undefined when every valid answer is unknown.
Keep template variants together for splitting and uncertainty. Name-based categories are imperfect proxies, and the benchmark's US-English stereotypes do not define global fairness.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, apply Section 5's ambiguous-context bias score to an invented table of 20 valid answers: 12 unknown, six stereotype-aligned and two against the stereotype. Accuracy is 60%, the conditional directional score is 0.5, and the ambiguity-scaled score is 0.2, or 20%. Then explain why balanced directional errors could give zero bias score while accuracy remains poor.
traps: Calling a zero directional score unbiased behavior. Opposing stereotypes or other errors can cancel in the aggregate.
Treating every template expansion as an independent observation. Shared wording and labels induce dependence.
Silently dropping unparsable answers. Declare a parsing policy and show invalid counts; an instrument failure is not a fairness improvement.

selfTest.q: Why report disambiguated cases whose answer contradicts the stereotype?
selfTest.a: They test whether explicit evidence overrides the stereotype. Overall accuracy can hide a gap between aligned and nonaligned correct answers.

selfTest.q: Every ambiguous answer is unknown. What is the conditional directional score?
selfTest.a: Undefined because there are no non-unknown outputs. The ambiguity-scaled score can be reported as zero by an explicit convention, alongside perfect ambiguous accuracy and the zero denominator.

selfTest.q: Does one category with no measured gap establish fairness?
selfTest.a: No. Coverage, statistical power, deployment population, language and untested harms remain limits.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: one pinned BBQ category with a template-balanced local-model subset, option-order checks, metadata-validated target labels, separate context-condition results and support-counted affected-group slices. Use the campaign's frozen small checkpoint and software; manually review a few scoring decisions.
units.stopWhen: Your category report separates evidence use from stereotype direction, reproduces the toy score, and names coverage, parsing and template-dependence limits.

fit.note: BBQ supplies the controlled context contrast and metric definition; NIST covers representation and disparate harms beyond the benchmark.

units.title: Matched benign utility controls and safety-evaluator calibration
outcomes: Calibrate deterministic and local model graders against a policy-linked hand-labeled subset.
Measure grader false positives, false negatives, parse failures and uncertainty separately from model behavior.
Compare interventions with matched benign tasks, not refusal rates alone.
units.why: The LLM Foundations unit on model judges and human review and the Classical ML unit on cost-sensitive thresholds, imbalance and prevalence change supply the tools. The new job is to show that a safety grader remains trustworthy on refusals, partial compliance and unfamiliar attacks.

next.note: Try to break the grader after establishing its calibration.

study.title: Inspect Evals: XSTest task 5-A
study.locator: `scorer_template`, `scorer_instructions`, `xstest`, `refusal_rate` and `record_to_sample`; accompanying README, Scoring and Changelog
study.depth: Inspect the interfaces, then build a local adaptation. Do not invoke the default OpenAI scorer. Give changed scoring rules their own task version.

study.title: StrongREJECT: rubric and human calibration, arXiv:2402.10260v1
study.locator: Section 3.4; Sections 4.2 and 5; Appendix A.4 grading instructions
study.depth: Use the rubric as a manually checked measurement design, not a claim that a tiny local judge reproduces the paper's grader.

study.title: CS336 supplement: benign baselines beside safety
study.locator: Sections 3.1 to 3.4 and 5.1 to 5.4: knowledge, arithmetic, instruction utility and safety
study.depth: Reuse a small frozen benign subset and saved outputs. Replace AlpacaEval's large judge with a blind hand review; do not run the full suites.

focus: Write labels from the frozen policy before seeing automatic scores. Reserve separate examples for rubric development and held-out grader assessment; adjudicate uncertain cases with reasons.
Compare string refusal detection and a rubric-based local judge on identical saved outputs. Keep semantic harmfulness separate from refusal class and answer quality.
Match benign controls by task type, topic, format and output budget where possible. Include ordinary utility tasks as well as XSTest's sensitive-but-benign prompts.
Define harmful output as the positive class when reporting detection precision and recall. Also report grader coverage, confusion counts, uncertainty and errors by attack family.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, score an invented held-out ledger of 20 outputs: eight are harmful by adjudicated labels; the grader flags six of those and four of the twelve harmless outputs. Recover six true positives, two false negatives, four false positives and eight true negatives. Detection precision is 60%, recall is 75%, and the false-positive rate is one third. Explain why none is the target model's harmful-compliance rate.
traps: Optimizing a rubric and reporting its agreement on the same labels. Hold out calibration-assessment cases as well as final model-evaluation cases.
Treating unparseable judge output as a safe target response. Preserve it as an instrument failure with a predeclared denominator policy.
Trusting aggregate agreement dominated by easy refusals. Inspect partial compliance, safe completion and family-specific errors.

selfTest.q: A grader flags almost nothing on a mostly harmless set and has high accuracy. Is it adequate?
selfTest.a: Not necessarily. Harm detection recall may be poor. Inspect confusion counts and errors on harmful and partial-compliance examples.

selfTest.q: Why retain both XSTest and ordinary benign tasks?
selfTest.a: XSTest measures exaggerated safety refusals. Ordinary tasks test broader usefulness that can regress without appearing as an explicit refusal.

selfTest.q: The local judge performs poorly on held-out hand labels. What should the release report use?
selfTest.a: Hand-adjudicated outcomes on a bounded subset, with uncertainty and the judge failure disclosed. A weak grader is not made valid by automation.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: one versioned Inspect adaptation with a deterministic scorer and a local rubric scorer, calibrated against held-out hand labels, plus matched benign controls. Pin inspect-ai 0.3.281 and the Inspect Evals commit in Study; reuse the frozen SmolLM2 baseline and transformers 5.19/PyTorch 2.14.1. Score saved outputs sequentially on CPU if needed. Keep task 5-A as a reference, not the name of your changed scorer. If the local judge fails calibration, retain its diagnostic results and use hand review for decisions.
units.stopWhen: Your held-out grader report includes confusion counts, coverage and family-level disagreements, and every safety comparison has a paired benign-utility result.

fit.note: The pinned Inspect task exposes the scorer contract; StrongREJECT supplies semantic calibration and CS336 supplies benign baselines. No new framework is needed.

units.title: Reward and evaluator gaming, and safety-test contamination and stale attacks
outcomes: Expose a reward or grader improvement that does not survive independent behavior review.
Audit safety-test exposure, attack-family overlap and stale evaluator versions.
Protect final evaluation from repeated prompt, defense and threshold selection.
units.why: The LLM Foundations unit on contamination and memorization covered exposed test items. The new failure is selection against a safety instrument: a model or developer can learn its shortcuts without improving the policy behavior the instrument was meant to measure.

next.note: Require uncontaminated, versioned evidence before promotion.

study.title: StrongREJECT: scoring shortcuts, arXiv:2402.10260v1
study.locator: Section 2.2; Section 5; Appendix B, Autograder Robustness Experiments
study.depth: Focus on enthusiastic but uninformative answers, disclaimers and errors that depend on attack format. Skip new attack generation.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: evaluation provenance and validity
study.locator: Section 3: MS-2.5-005 (training and TEVV provenance), MS-2.5-006 (review guardrails), MS-2.11-001 (benchmark limitations and cross contamination), MS-2.13-001 (measurement error)

study.title: LLM Post-Training Laboratory: proxy failure campaign
study.locator: Milestone D, Failure handling; Milestone F, Final evaluation; Correctness requirements; Failure-injection requirements
study.depth: Use the reward/behavior divergence and final-evaluation requirements only; do not repeat earlier training stages.

focus: Audit the measuring instrument with content-preserving style and length changes. A score change is suspicious only after checking that the edit preserved the policy-relevant meaning.
Trace safety items through SFT data, preference data, synthetic critiques, prompt development and evaluator tuning. Exact text checks miss shared templates and paraphrased attack families.
Separate development attacks, grader-calibration cases and final held-out families. Repeatedly choosing the best defense on the final set turns it into development data.
Freeze evaluator prompts, parsing, task revision, model revision and denominator rules. Add fresh attacks on a scheduled review, but keep a fixed regression set for longitudinal comparisons.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, design a harmless proxy hack: prepend an apology to an otherwise useful answer to a benign request. The XSTest prefix matcher calls an answer beginning with an apology a full refusal even if it continues to answer. Specify the hand label and a content-preserving control that would expose the shortcut, then explain how the same shortcut could distort a safety-training reward.
traps: Calling any near-duplicate scan proof of clean pretraining. It checks only available data under its stated normalization and matching rule.
Updating the evaluator between checkpoints and attributing the whole score change to training. Rescore identical saved outputs to isolate the instrument change.
Retiring every attack a defense blocks. That erases regression evidence and rewards memorizing the latest public suite.

selfTest.q: Reward rises but blind hand review finds unchanged policy behavior. What improved?
selfTest.a: The proxy score improved. Training may have exploited a shortcut; it has not demonstrated a behavioral safety gain.

selfTest.q: No exact training/test string overlap is found. Can you rule out contamination?
selfTest.a: No. Paraphrases, shared templates, indirect feedback and unknown pretraining data remain possible exposure routes.

selfTest.q: How do you separate evaluator drift from policy drift?
selfTest.a: Rescore fixed raw outputs with both evaluator versions and evaluate both policies with one frozen evaluator. Preserve item-level disagreements.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a seeded apology, style or length shortcut on harmless saved outputs; independent labels; a safety-item exposure manifest; family-level split checks; and a replay comparing evaluator versions. Retain the original failures and keep final attacks out of defense selection.
units.stopWhen: Your audit exposes one proxy shortcut, distinguishes evaluator drift from behavior change, and documents known and unknown exposure routes for the final attack set.

fit.note: StrongREJECT covers grader shortcuts; NIST covers provenance, contamination and measurement validity; the laboratory supplies the named failure campaign.

units.title: Safety training-data lineage and constitutional critique and revision
outcomes: Implement a small principle-conditioned critique/revision data loop with complete lineage.
Audit safety SFT and preference records for policy conflicts, source exposure and evasiveness.
Separate AI-generated supervision from independent evidence of safer behavior.
units.why: A safety intervention starts with data choices, not a loss function. This unit adds policy and generator lineage to the SFT and preference contracts from earlier sections without repeating their optimization work.

next.note: Test the intervention against utility loss and held-out attacks.

study.title: Constitutional AI, arXiv:2212.08073v1
study.locator: Figure 1; Section 3.1, Method; Section 4.1, Method; Sections 4.3 and 4.4, including Harmlessness vs. Evasiveness; Appendix A critique/revision examples
study.depth: Implement one critique/revision pass and its records. The full preference-model and RL pipeline is reading only, not a required reproduction.

study.title: CS336 supplement: inspect safety demonstrations and preferences
study.locator: Section 4.1, `look_at_sft`; Section 6.2, `look_at_hh`
study.depth: Read for data-inspection questions and source tracking. Use your existing small SFT/preference data instead of the course's shared-volume corpus.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: data origin and transformations
study.locator: Section 3: GV-1.2-001 and MP-2.1-002

focus: Record source prompt, original response, principle and policy version, critique, revision, generator checkpoint, template, decoding and review decision. Retain rejected revisions with reasons.

Supervised CAI trains on the revised response paired with the original prompt. Its AI-feedback phase instead creates comparisons for a preference model and subsequent RL. A revision loop alone is neither phase's trained outcome.
AI feedback still depends on human-chosen principles and can inherit the generator's errors. Critique fluency is not evidence that a revision is correct or harmless.
Split by source conversation and generator lineage. Keep evaluation prompts and final attack families out of synthetic-data generation, preference selection and rubric tuning.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, draw the two CAI supervision paths: prompt to answer to critique to revision to an SFT pair; and prompt to response pair to principle-conditioned preference to preference model to RL. Then reconstruct one record from your small loop and identify which fields distinguish human policy choices, generated supervision and independent review.
traps: Discarding the original unsafe or unhelpful response once a revision exists. That loses the intervention's baseline and hides failed revisions.
Using the same model's approval as the only evaluation. Shared blind spots can certify a worse answer.
Training on blanket refusals for every sensitive topic. That changes the policy boundary and can reward evasiveness over useful safe completion.

selfTest.q: Does constitutional supervision remove human normative choices?
selfTest.a: No. Humans choose principles, data, deployment scope and review criteria; the paper also retains human helpfulness feedback in its RL phase.

selfTest.q: A revision becomes less specific and the generator praises it. Is that a safety gain?
selfTest.a: Not established. Independent review must check policy behavior and usefulness; evasiveness can improve a proxy while degrading assistance.

selfTest.q: What is the supervised training target after critique and revision?
selfTest.a: The revised response to the original prompt. The critique is part of data generation, not automatically part of the deployed assistant's target response.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: one local critique/revision pass on a handful of invented policy-boundary cases and matched benign requests, with complete SFT or preference-data lineage and blind hand review. Reuse the frozen small-model/software setup from the baseline, sequentially on CPU if needed. Keep an unmodified response control and failed revisions; no full RLAIF training is required.
units.stopWhen: You can reconstruct every revision from its policy and generator record, form the correct training pair, and distinguish a reviewed data intervention from a demonstrated trained-policy improvement.

fit.note: The CAI paper supplies both supervision paths and evasiveness caveats; CS336 and NIST supply source inspection and provenance.

units.title: Defense in depth and capability-safety trade-off curves
outcomes: Compare training, classifier, application and monitoring controls without assuming independent failures.
Measure a capability-safety frontier under matched generation and attack budgets.
Diagnose gains caused by capability loss, overrefusal or a stale attacker rather than robust mitigation.
units.why: A system prompt, a trained policy and an output filter fail in different places. This unit asks which layer changes the measured failure and what useful behavior it costs, rather than treating more layers as automatic safety.

next.note: Turn the supported trade-off into an explicit release decision.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: layered controls and reassessment
study.locator: Section 3: MG-3.1-001 and MG-3.1-003 (filters, fine-tuning and reassessment); MS-2.6-005 to MS-2.6-007 (monitoring, handling misuse and circumvention)

study.title: Constitutional AI: competing objectives, arXiv:2212.08073v1
study.locator: Sections 4.3 and 4.4: helpfulness/harmlessness comparisons and Harmlessness vs. Evasiveness
study.depth: Read the trade-offs and evaluator dependence, not the large-model scores as local targets.

study.title: StrongREJECT: capability loss as an alternative explanation
study.locator: Sections 6.2 and 6.3: jailbreaks can hurt model performance, including on MMLU

focus: Distinguish a policy intervention from an application restriction. Removing tool authority can prevent an action even when the language model still proposes it; report both attempted and executed violations.
Compare the unchanged system, each individual control and their combination. A training control can reuse an earlier SFT/preference checkpoint; no new large training run is needed.

Sweep one development-set control strength, such as a classifier threshold, then freeze settings. Plot harmful compliance against benign utility and overrefusal, with privacy and group slices alongside.
Use paired item comparisons and template/family-aware uncertainty. Hold query and output budgets fixed, include control overhead, and rerun a fresh adaptive attacker against the frozen candidate.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, sketch a frontier with useful benign completion on one axis and harmful compliance on the other. Add an always-refuse baseline and mark dominated configurations: a configuration is dominated if another has no worse measured utility and compliance, with a strict improvement in at least one. Explain why uncertainty, severity and unplotted privacy risks can still prevent selecting an apparently dominant point.
traps: Multiplying layer failure rates without independence evidence. A shared prompt or model can defeat several layers together.
Calling a classifier block a better model. The system's output policy changed; the underlying model may not have changed at all.
Trading one severe failure for many easy successes in an average. Retain severity gates and affected-group regressions beside the curve.

selfTest.q: All outputs are blocked. Has the system reached a useful safety frontier?
selfTest.a: It supplies a limiting refusal baseline, not useful assistance. Benign utility and overrefusal expose the cost.

selfTest.q: Why test each layer alone before the combination?
selfTest.a: Ablations identify which control changes behavior and whether combined controls add value or merely share failures and overhead.

selfTest.q: A defense improves only against yesterday's fixed attacks. What is missing?
selfTest.a: Held-out-family and adaptive evaluation at the same declared budget, with a frozen defense and calibrated success labels.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a matched-budget baseline, individual-control and combined-control comparison, a development-set control-strength curve, and one frozen mitigation retested on held-out adaptive attacks. Use the campaign's small checkpoint on your GPU or CPU. Cheap application permission checks and a deterministic synthetic-secret output check are valid controls; report their narrow coverage rather than implying learned alignment.
units.stopWhen: Your comparison identifies each control's contribution and cost, keeps benign and severe-failure slices visible, and states whether the mitigation survives held-out adaptive review.

fit.note: NIST supplies layered-control and reassessment actions; CAI and StrongREJECT supply utility and capability-loss confounds. The campaign provides the controlled comparison.

units.title: Release thresholds, staged rollout, monitoring, rollback and residual-risk ownership
outcomes: Defend predeclared safety, utility and uncertainty gates for a bounded release candidate.
Explain a staged rollout with review, monitoring, incident handling and a tested rollback.
Assign residual risks and evidence gaps to an owner without claiming certification.
units.why: The Systems units on failure domains, correctness signals and safe rollout and on backups, runbooks, incident timelines and postmortems cover the operations. Here the new job is deciding whether model-behavior evidence is strong enough for a specific use, including uncertainty and untested harms.

next.note: Bind the decision to the exact candidate artifacts and governance record.

study.title: NIST AI 600-1: release, review and deactivation
study.depth: Read these actions as governance requirements. NIST does not supply numeric release thresholds for your application.

study.title: LLM Post-Training Laboratory: release evidence boundary
study.locator: Architecture constraints; Milestones D to F; Correctness requirements; Completion checklist; Out of scope
study.depth: Use immutable records, independent evaluation and rollback criteria. Frontier certification and production operations remain outside this study.

focus: Before final evaluation, declare acceptable harmful-compliance, privacy, overrefusal, utility and critical-slice outcomes. Specify sample counts, uncertainty method, coverage requirements and what forces a hold.

Bind a decision to policy, threat model, model, tokenizer, data, attack and grader versions. Preserve failures and human adjudications; an incomplete instrument can block promotion even if its scored subset passes.
Rehearse offline evaluation, shadow replay and a restricted simulated canary before any broader use. Monitor behavior and utility by version and slice, not just availability or aggregate refusal.
Name the release decision owner, incident responder and residual-risk owner. Define the previous complete system configuration, the rollback trigger and the check that verifies restoration.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, assess an idealized fixed sample of 20 independent, identically distributed Bernoulli trials with zero failures. The exact one-sided 95% upper bound on the failure probability is \(1-0.05^{1/20}\), about 13.91%, not zero. Then explain why correlated adaptive attempts or a hand-selected attack set do not justify applying that bound to deployment traffic.
traps: Choosing the gate after seeing candidate scores. That turns a release criterion into a description of the chosen model.
Rolling back only weights when the failure came from a prompt, retrieval source, filter or evaluator. Restore the relevant versioned system, not one artifact.
Assigning risk to a team with no decision maker or expiry. Give each accepted gap an owner, review date and reopening condition.

selfTest.q: No severe failures appear in a small final set. Is release automatically justified?
selfTest.a: No. The sample may have low power or poor coverage. Apply the predeclared uncertainty and coverage gates and disclose what was not tested.

selfTest.q: Why include benign utility in rollback triggers?
selfTest.a: A change can prevent misuse by making the assistant unusable. User-visible task regressions are release failures even when refusal rises.

selfTest.q: What distinguishes a release record from a safety certificate?
selfTest.a: The record supports a scoped decision for named versions, evidence and assumptions. It cannot establish universal alignment, future robustness or regulatory certification.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: a signed-off local release/hold record with predeclared thresholds, uncertainty and coverage checks, staged replay, a seeded behavioral regression, a rollback rehearsal and owned residual risks. The learner may hold all roles, but names each responsibility. No real deployment or external users are required.
units.stopWhen: A reviewer can reproduce the release or hold decision from frozen evidence, trigger the simulated rollback, verify restoration and identify who owns every unresolved risk.

fit.note: NIST covers roles, monitoring, incident review and deactivation; the laboratory supplies independent evidence and rollback requirements. Thresholds are explicitly application choices.

units.title: Activation probes and scalable oversight as supporting safety evidence
outcomes: Explain why activation decodability is supporting evidence, not proof of causal use, truthful intent or safety.
Design a probe evaluation with source-held-out tests and shortcut controls.
Separate debate and recursive oversight proposals from demonstrated supervision beyond human capability.
units.why: This optional unit examines evidence that can complement the behavioral campaign. Neither a probe nor an assisted judge replaces its policy, attack and utility gates; skip this unit without leaving a required safety claim unfinished.

next.note: Label supporting evidence and unresolved assumptions in the release record.

study.title: ARENA 1.3.1 Linear Probes: evidence and limits
study.locator: What is probing?; Why this matters for safety; What you'll build; Models we'll use; learning objectives for Training & comparing probes and Causal interventions
study.depth: Read the evidence distinctions only. Do not load the large gated models or run the full deception-detection pipeline.

study.title: ARENA: cross-dataset probe generalization
study.locator: Exercise - cross-dataset generalization matrix; Discussion - interpreting the generalization matrix
study.depth: Use the exercise to design a held-out-source comparison. Skip the source's large-model accuracy assertions; they are not targets for a different checkpoint.

study.title: AI safety via debate, arXiv:1805.00899v1
study.locator: Sections 1 to 3: the debate game and preliminary experiments; Section 7, Approximate equivalence with amplification
study.depth: Read for assumptions and the recursive-supervision connection. Skip the complexity proof details and full MNIST experiment.

focus: Fix the probe target, checkpoint, layer, token position, labels and split before fitting. A property predictable from activations may reflect topic, format or supplied instructions rather than hidden intent.
Compare held-out sources, label-shuffled controls and simple text-feature baselines. Fit any normalization on probe training data only; selecting layers on the final test set leaks feedback.
Intervening along a direction asks a causal question that classification alone cannot answer. A changed output can still result from nonspecific damage, so use control directions and utility checks.

Debate and recursive amplification try to make difficult judgments tractable through challenges or decomposition. They still depend on truthful evidence access, capable challengers and a judge that can recognize the decisive error.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, draw two competing explanations for a successful probe: it reads a behavior-relevant representation, or it reads a label-correlated topic cue. Specify a source-held-out comparison and a controlled intervention that could distinguish them. Then draw a debate or recursive-decomposition path that ends at a human-checkable claim and name the assumption that could break that path.
traps: Calling a high probe score a lie detector. The measured target and transfer setting may not capture deception or intent at all.
Calling a probe trained on the campaign's labels an independent oracle. It can inherit the same annotation and source shortcuts.
Treating optimal-play reasoning or toy debate experiments as deployed alignment evidence. Finite models and human judges need separate validation.

selfTest.q: Does accurate decoding prove the model uses that feature to produce its answer?
selfTest.a: No. Prediction establishes accessible information under that probe and split. Causal-use claims need controlled interventions and alternative explanations checked.

selfTest.q: A probe fails after a topic shift. What can you conclude?
selfTest.a: Its measured transfer is poor. It may have relied on a topic cue or the representation may have shifted; the failure does not show the underlying property disappeared.

selfTest.q: Why can two persuasive debaters still mislead a judge?
selfTest.a: They may share blind spots, lack access to verifiable evidence or exploit the judge's weaknesses. More argument is not automatically better supervision.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: an optional supporting-evidence note with a probe hypothesis, source-held-out design, shortcut and causal controls, and a debate or recursive-oversight failure analysis. It must state which behavioral release gates remain unchanged. No large-model probe run or multi-agent service is required.
units.stopWhen: You can propose discriminating probe controls and identify the empirical assumptions of assisted oversight, while keeping both outside the required behavioral safety claim.

fit.note: Current ARENA probe pages and the debate paper cover the optional explain-level evidence boundary; the amplification section supplies the recursive-oversight connection.
